title: Why Can Wind Ground the Giant Thanksgiving Parade Balloons?
fb_caption: This Thanksgiving, the giant balloons are not flying over New York. The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been moved to Saturday because of a storm. So why would wind stop a parade that usually marches through rain and cold? A giant balloon is several stories tall and acts like a sail, wind force grows about four times when wind speed doubles, and tall buildings can funnel sudden gusts around corners. New York City's limits for the big balloons are 23 mph sustained and 34 mph in gusts. Which balloon is your all-time favorite? Tell us below.
engagement_comment: Would you hold a line on a giant balloon in a 30 mph gust? Reply YES or NO WAY, and tell us which balloon you'd want to fly!

Large-balloon wind limits in New York City: sustained winds over 23 mph, gusts over 34 mph [Verified: 1 opened source (NBC News 2026) + 2019 reports seen as search summaries]: NBC News live blog 25 Nov 2026 ("sustained winds over 23 mph or gusts above 34 mph for large balloons"); AP 2019 as carried by Fortune (search summary only, pages not opened): https://fortune.com/2019/11/28/macys-thanksgiving-day-parade-2019-balloons and CBS New York 2019: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/macys-thanksgiving-day-parade-2019-balloons (older reports word it "and", NBC 2026 "or": the script only names the two numbers)

The balloons were already being inflated when the move was announced; officials said they would be deflated and prepared again for Saturday [Inflating: 2 sources (WYFF "well on the way to being inflated"; ABC7). Deflating + back to New Jersey: ABC7 only, so worded as "officials said"]: ABC7; WYFF

In windy years the balloons have flown lower than usual [2 sources]: WYFF 25 Nov 2026; Fox 5 NY 2019: https://www.fox5ny.com/news/macys-thanksgiving-day-parade-2019-balloons-fly-just-lower-than-usual

beats.text: This Thanksgiving, the giant balloons are not flying over New York. The one hundredth Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been moved to Saturday, because of a storm.
This parade usually marches on through rain and cold. So why would wind stop it? Follow the questions.

overlays.text:
WHY WOULD WIND
STOP A PARADE?

items: RAIN AND COLD: IT USUALLY MARCHES ON

beats.text: First question. Why not just march? Because of the balloons. A giant parade balloon is filled with helium and stands several stories tall. To the wind, that is not a toy. It is a sail.

items: TO THE WIND, IT IS A SAIL

beats.text: But why can't the handlers just hold on? Each giant balloon has around eighty to a hundred of them. The trouble is the math. Double the wind speed, and the push is about four times stronger.
So why not fly them lower? In windy years, they have. But a city makes its own gusts. Tall buildings can squeeze the wind and fire it around corners.

So where is the line? New York City draws it. For the big balloons, the limits are twenty-three miles an hour sustained, and thirty-four in gusts. Officials said this storm's forecast gusts were well beyond that.

items: NEW YORK CITY LIMITS, BIG BALLOONS

beats.text: Only once before, in nineteen seventy-one, did weather keep the balloons down. This time, they were already being inflated. Officials said they would be let down, and readied again for Saturday.
Takeaway: if wind can push around a balloon the size of a building, it can launch your trampoline, your patio umbrella and your yard inflatables. Tie them down before the storm.

items: TIE THEM DOWN BEFORE THE STORM

beats.text: Which balloon is your all-time favorite? Tell us in the comments, and send this to someone who never misses the parade. Because this Thanksgiving, the wind decided: the giant balloons stay down.
